utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case IT-95-8-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Kolundzija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If it please the Court, Dirk Ryneveld on behalf of the Prosecutor, and with me is Kapila Waidyaratne, and we're prepared to proceed this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: May it please the Court, on behalf of the accused -- okay now? May it please the Court, on behalf of the accused, Dusan Vucicevic of Chicago, and I'm indeed privileged to be before this Trial Chamber, especially before the Presiding Judge, Judge May. It's going to be here, Judge May, and we're looking forward to justice, a swift kind of justice, Your Honour. And the Honourable Judges of this Trial Chamber, I would ask you for a speedy trial for my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. The purpose of this appearance is for an initial appearance which has been adjourned, and it's basically for the accused to plead to the indictment. Now, we have had an application from the Prosecution to amend the indictment in relation to correcting the spelling of the name of the accused, and also to amend the place and date of birth. Mr. Ryneveld, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vucicevic, any --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Defence has no objection to those requests to correct the technicalities of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. In that case, the indictment will be amended accordingly. Before the indictment is put, the Trial Chamber must be satisfied firstly that the accused has received a copy of it in a language which he understands, and that his counsel has had the opportunity of going through it with him, and that he understands its contents. Mr. Vucicevic, may we take it that that has all been done?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: While you're on your feet, as you know, the accused does have the right to have the indictment read out to him in open court in full, but he can also waive that right, and we would ask you what the position is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I have not consulted my client about it. Your Honour, if you would indulge me for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would like to go and ask him if he wants it read out or whether we can just go straight to the counts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, I will. Your Honour, we would prefer the indictment read in open court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Let that be done. (Trial Chamber confers)

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Richard J. Goldstone, Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to his authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (hereinafter "the Statute"), charges: From about 24 May to about 30 August, 1992, Serb forces unlawfully seized and confined more than 3.000 Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats from the opstina Prijedor, in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in inhumane conditions, under armed guards, in the Keraterm "camp", located in a former ceramics factory and storage area complex located just outside the town of Prijedor. As set forth below, detainees at Keraterm camp were killed, sexually assaulted, tortured, beaten, and otherwise subjected to cruel and inhuman treatment. Unless otherwise specified, all acts and omissions set forth in this indictment took place between 24 May and 30 August 1992. At all times relevant to this indictment, a state of armed conflict and partial occupation existed in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. All acts or omissions set forth as grave breaches recognised by Article 2 of the Statute and violations of the laws or customs of war pursuant to Article 3 of the Statute occurred during that armed conflict and partial occupation. All of the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat detainees at Keraterm camp, and the Bosnian Muslims and Croats of the opstina Prijedor referred to in this indictment were, at all relevant times, persons protected by the Geneva Conventions of 1949. All of the accused in this indictment were required to abide by the mandate of the laws and customs governing the conduct of armed conflict, including the Geneva Conventions of 1949. In each paragraph charging torture, the acts were committed by, or at the instigation of, or with the consent or acquiescence of, an official or person acting in an official capacity, and for one or more of the following purposes: To obtain information or a confession from the victim or a third person; to punish the victim for an act the victim or a third person committed or was suspected of having committed, to intimidate or coerce the victim or a third person; and/or for any reason based upon discrimination of any kind. In each paragraph charging crimes against humanity, crimes recognised by Article 5 of the Statute, the alleged acts or omissions were part of a widespread or large-scale or systematic attack directed against a civilian population. The term "Serb" refers to persons of Serbian descent who were either Bosnian citizens or citizens from any other part of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: The persons accused in this indictment were commanders, guards, interrogators, and others responsible for the conditions and mistreatment of detainees in Keraterm camp. The following three men were shift commanders who each supervised one of the three shifts of guards that operated the camp. As shift commanders, when on duty, they were in positions of superior authority to all persons within the camp, second only to the camp commander, among which: Dragan Kolundzija a/k/a "Kole", born 19 December 1959, in the town of Bosanski Novi, in Bosnia-Herzegovina. In addition to the accused described above who regularly performed duties in Keraterm camp, others frequently entered the camp and killed, beat or otherwise abused detainees. While they were in the camp, they were subject to the authority of Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Dragan Fustar, and Dragan Kolundzija. Paragraphs 1 through 10 are re-alleged and incorporated into each of the charges set forth below. Charges: II. Criminal Responsibility In The Capacity As A Superior Authority. Accused: Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Dragan Fustar, and Dragan Kolundzija in their capacity as superiors. During the operation of Keraterm camp, the vast majority of the detainees were held in the Keraterm factory building in what were previously four storage areas known as "room 1, room 2, room 3, and room 4." The overcrowded conditions in the rooms were extreme, to the extent that on many occasions the detainees could not lie down. Facilities for personal hygiene were all but nonexistent. The toilet facilities were completely inadequate so that frequently the toilet area was awash in urine and faeces. The detainees were fed starvation rations once a day, with little time to eat. The little water they received was ordinarily foul. Detainees had no changes of clothing and no bedding. They received little or no medical care. On a regular basis, camp guards and others who came to the camp to abuse the detainees, all of whom were subordinate to Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Dragan Fustar and Dragan Kolundzija, subjected the detainees to physical violence, constant humiliation, degradation, inhuman conditions, and fear of death. Hundreds of detainees were killed by the guards and others. Severe beatings were commonplace. All manner of weapons were used during these beatings, including wooden batons, metal rods, baseball bats, lengths of thick industrial cable that had metal balls affixed to the end, rifle butts and knives. The killings, beatings, sexual assaults, and other cruel and humiliating actions were committed on every shift and were often inflicted in full view of the other detainees. Many detainees, whose identities are known and unknown, did not survive. The corpses of detainees were piled next to a garbage area adjacent to room 4 prior to their removal from the camp. With respect to the acts described above and each act or omission charged hereafter in this indictment, except those charges where one or more of these accused is separately charged, Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Dragan Fustar, and Dragan Kolundzija knew or had reason to know that persons in positions of subordinate authority to them were about to commit those acts, or had already committed those acts, and failed either to take the necessary and reasonable steps to prevent those acts or to punish the perpetrators after the acts had been committed. Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Dragan Fustar, and Dragan Kolundzija are criminally responsible for the killing of Keraterm camp detainees by their respective subordinates and others subject to their authority, including the killings described in paragraphs 14, 15, 17 to 20, 24 and 25, and thereby committed: Count 13.4.1: grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, wilful killings, recognised by Articles 2(a) and 7(3) of the Statute; Count 13.4.2: violations of the laws or customs of war, murder, recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute and by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions; Count 13.4.3, crimes against humanity, murder, recognised by Articles 5(a) and 7(3) of the Statute. Count 13.6: Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Dragan Fustar, and Dragan Kolundzija are criminally responsible for the wilful causing of great suffering to all the Keraterm detainees, including those acts or omissions described in paragraphs 14, 16, 19, 20, 23, 26 to 29, and 31 to 33 by their respective subordinates and others subject to their authority and thereby committed grave breaches recognised by Article 2(c) and 7(3) of the Statute. Count 13.7: Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Dragan Fustar, and Dragan Kolundzija are criminally responsible for the commission of outrages upon the personal dignity of all the Keraterm detainees, including those described in paragraphs 14 to 33, by their respective subordinates and others subject to their authority, and thereby committed violations of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute and Article 3(1)(c) of the Geneva Conventions. Count 13.8: Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Dragan Fustar, and Dragan Kolundzija are criminally responsible for the acts of their respective subordinates and others subject to their authority, who subjected the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat detainees of Keraterm, including those described in paragraphs 14 to 33, to persecution on political, racial, and/or religious grounds, and thereby committed a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(h) and 7(3) of the Statute. Count 13.9: Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Dragan Fustar, and Dragan Kolundzija are criminally responsible for the acts or omissions of their respective subordinates and others subject to their authority, in subjecting the detainees of Keraterm, including those described in paragraphs 14 to 33, to inhumane acts and treatment, and thereby committed a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(i) and 7(3) of the Statute. III: Individual criminal responsibility. Accused, Dragan Kolundzija. 14.1: About 20 July, 1992, detainees from an area of the opstina Prijedor known as "Brdo," which included the villages of Hambarine, Carakovo, Rakovcani, Biscani, and Rizvanovici, were brought to Keraterm camp. The detainees from the Brdo area were crowded into room 3. The previous occupants of room 3 had earlier been transferred to other rooms. About 24 July 1992, the detainees in Room 3 were not allowed out of the room. During the day and early evening, machine guns were set up in front of the rooms. That night soldiers were brought into the camp and formed a semicircle around room 3. Later that night, the guards and soldiers, including Zoran Zigic, began firing into a room with machine guns and heavy calibre guns. The firing continued off and on over a period of several hours, alternating between continuous fire and short bursts of fire. The fire was directed toward room 3. However, some of the bullets went into at least one of the other rooms. On that evening, Dragan Kolundzija was the guard shift commander. He gave orders that the other rooms were not to be fired on. He gave no orders that room 3 was not to be fired on. Dragan Kolundzija, as guard shift commander, Zoran Zigic, and camp guards and others whose identities are unknown, participated in the murder of at least 140 men from the Brdo area detained in Room 3, and thereby committed 14.4.1, a grave breach, wilful killing, recognised by Article 2(a) and 7(1) of the Statute, and, with respect to Dragan Kolundzija, also Article 7(3) of the Statute. Count 14.4.2, a violation of the laws and customs of war, murder, recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute, and with respect to Dragan Kolundzija, also Article 7(3) of the Statute, and by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions; and Count 14.4.3: a crime against humanity, murder, recognised by Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute, and, with respect to Dragan Kolundzija, also Article 7(3) of the Statute. 14.5: Dragan Kolundzija, Zoran Zigic and camp guards, and others whose identities are unknown, participated in wounding, by gunfire, approximately 50 men from the "Brdo" area detained in room 3, including Safet Crljenkovic, Dervis Drljenkovic, Ramo Crljenkovic, and Alija Hrapic. Dragan Kolundzija, as a superior responsible for the acts of his subordinates and by direct participation, Zoran Zigic, and camp guards and others whose identities are unknown thereby committed: Count 14.5.1: a grave breach, wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health, recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(1) of the Statute, and, with respect to Dragan Kolundzija, also Article 7(3) of the Statute; Count 14.5.2, a violation of the laws and customs of war, cruel treatment, recognised by Articles 3 and 7(1), and with respect to Dragan Kolundzija, also 7(3) of the Statute, and by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions; and Count 14.5.3, a crime against humanity, inhumane acts, recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute, and, with respect Dragan Kolundzija, also Article 7(3) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That concludes the indictment as far as the accused is concerned. Thank you. Dragan Kolundzija, would you stand, please. I'm now going to put the counts of the indictment to you for you to plead to them. In each case, kindly plead guilty or not guilty to each, and confine your answers to that. The first counts, as you've heard, allege criminal responsibility in your capacity as a superior. The first three counts are under paragraph 13 of the indictment and relate to the killing of detainees at the Keraterm camp. It is alleged that you, Dusica Sikirica, Damir Dosen, and Dragan Fustar were criminally responsible, in your capacity as superiors, for the killing of detainees by your subordinates and others subject to your authority, and that you thereby committed the following offences. The first count alleges grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, wilful killings, recognised by Articles 2(a) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next count alleges violations of the laws or customs of war, murder, recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute and by Article (3)(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The third count alleges crimes against humanity, murder, recognised by Articles 5(a) and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next four counts are also under paragraph 13, and they relate to the ill treatment of detainees at the camp. At paragraph 13(6), the count alleges that Dusko Sikirica, Damir Dosen, Dragan Fustar, and you were criminally responsible for wilfully causing great suffering to all the Keraterm detainees by your subordinates and others subject to your authority, and you thereby committed grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions recognised by Articles 2(c) and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next count alleges that you and the others named already were criminally responsible for the commission of outrages upon personal dignity of all the Keraterm detainees by your subordinates and others subject to your authority, and you thereby committed violations of the laws or customs of war recognised by Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute and Article 3(1)(c) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next count alleges that you and the others already named were criminally responsible for the acts of your subordinates and others subject to your authority who subjected the Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croat detainees at Keraterm to persecution on political, racial, and/or religious grounds, and you thereby committed a crime against humanity, recognised by Articles 5(h) and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next count alleges that you and the others already named were criminally responsible for the acts or omissions of your subordinates and others subject to your authority in subjecting the detainees of Keraterm to inhumane acts and treatment, and thereby you committed a crime against humanity recognised by Articles 5(i) and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The remaining counts allege individual criminal responsibility. They are pleaded in paragraph 14. They relate to events which took place on or about the 24th of July, 1992, in the Keraterm camp. In paragraph 14(4), it is alleged that you, as guard shift commander, Zoran Zigic, camp guards, and others whose identities are unknown, participated in the murder of at least 140 men from the Brdo area detained in room 3. It is alleged that you, being a superior responsible for the acts of your subordinates, and by direct participation, thereby committed the following offences: 14.4.1: a grave breach, wilful killing, recognised by Articles 2(a) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next count alleges a violation of the laws and customs of war, murder, recognised by Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute, and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next count alleges a crime against humanity, murder recognised by Articles 5(a), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next counts allege that you and Zoran Zigic and camp guards and others whose identity are unknown, participated in wounding, by gunfire, approximately 50 men from the "Brdo" area detained in Room 3. You, as a superior responsible for the acts of your subordinates, and by direct participation have thereby committed the following offences: 14.5.1: a grave breach, wilfully causing great suffering or serious injury to body or health, recognised by Articles 2(c), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next count, a violation of the laws and customs of war, cruel treatment, recognised by Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute, and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next count alleges a crime against humanity, inhumane acts, recognised by Articles 5(i), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That is all, as far as the indictment is concerned, and you may sit down. There are various matters I should deal with, I am reminded by the legal officer, concerned with formal orders as to disclosure, and preliminary motions. First of all, that the Prosecution should disclose all supporting material and any statements of the accused in a language the accused understands within 30 days; that is, by the 12th of August. And any preliminary motions under Rule 72 must be filed within 30 days of that disclosure. There are various applications, Mr. Ryneveld, we understand, in relation to the amending of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: There are indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Clearly, those orders which I've made will have to be followed despite any applications there may be about amendment to the indictment. The position is this: That this Trial Chamber will be here until the 6th of August, but thereafter we shall be in recess for a month. Now, if there are any matters which have to be dealt with, they should be dealt with, if possible, before then, bearing in mind that we shall be dealing with the trial of another case. So time is tight.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Thank you, Mr. President. I understand that the disclosure materials are ready now, and I'm sure that those matters can be dealt with as expeditiously as possible. The other matters which are extant depend, of course, on the availability and the time of rulings for matters that are ex parte. There are some matters yet outstanding concerning amendment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are they before the confirming Judge?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: They are indeed, yes, Mr. President. We are awaiting his pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So there are no other matters as far as the Prosecution are concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If I just may consult with my colleague, just to make sure, out of an abundance of caution. No matters before this Chamber at this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will need to fix a date for a Status Conference, which must be held within the next 120 days. We would hope to hear it rather before then in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I neglected to point out I am here on behalf of Mr. Niemann, who is out of the country, and it may well be that Mr. Niemann will certainly be there for a status conference, but whatever date the court chooses is acceptable to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I turn to the Defence. Mr. Vucicevic, are there any matters you want to raise today?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm somewhat surprised with the Prosecutor's statement, that maybe something has been submitted to the confirming Judge in the interim, that I have not received a copy. But my understanding is that the motion asking for an amended indictment and rejoinder of the accused has been rejected and I haven't received any other copy. I'm of the understanding that the confirming Judge has advised that any matters as to amendment be brought before this Chamber or the other chamber, as you know, hearing the other cases where the Prosecution has asked the rejoinder. So I was indeed very happy that you advised the Prosecutor to bring any amendments before this Chamber having heard an indictment that is rather, indeed, a very broad attempt to charge all the participants in the actions that have happened in the Keraterm Camp. And I would like to stress that if there was ever a good Samaritan, so far that had appeared before this court, that would be this gentleman here, Mr. Dragan Kolundzija. And what I'm stating from the statements that were enclosed as to the amended complaint that was thus far rejected. I would ask the Prosecutor to, in his attempt, wherever he wishes to bring this, to specify what were the acts of the accused so as to help this Trial Chamber and allow us to prepare a proper defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to that in due course. What we'll do is fix a date for another status conference, and perhaps the legal officer could assist us. (Trial Chamber confers)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn this case until the next status conference, which will be on Tuesday, the 28th of September, at 2.30 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 3.12 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of September, 1999, at 2.30 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
